trace.final_message:
Added `rosterkit/notices.py` with `build_notice(student, marks)`. It returns text like `Ana Rivera missed 2 day(s): 2026-03-02, 2026-03-09.` A helper, `absent_days`, picks the absent marks and sorts their dates. Both raise `ValueError` if any mark belongs to a different student, and `build_notice` also raises it when there are no absences. Only the status `absent` counts, so late and excused days are ignored.

Added `tests/test_notices.py` with three tests: dates in order, a foreign mark rejected, and no absences rejected. `make check` passes with twenty-nine tests, and `make lint` is clean.

The work is committed as `c1ba6fc`. My first commit went in while one line was still too long and a bad edit had broken the code. I fixed both and amended that commit before finishing, so the history holds a single commit.

I did not run `git diff` for a separate review before committing. I only checked `git diff --stat`.
